elements.element: Governing law is the laws of the State of New York
elements.evidence: 28.1 "governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York"

elements.element: Exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County
elements.evidence: 28.1 "the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction"

elements.element: Governing law and forum form a permitted corresponding pair (NY law with NY courts)
elements.evidence: NY law paired with New York County courts in the same sentence of 28.1

elements.element: Exclusivity of the chosen forum is not diluted by a carve-out permitting suit in other courts
elements.evidence: 28.2 "Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction" (untouched)

elements.element: Alternative: Delaware or California law with Delaware/California courts
elements.evidence: Clause selects "the laws of the State of New York", not Delaware or California

elements.element: Alternative: laws of England and Wales with the courts of London
elements.evidence: No reference to England and Wales or London in the rendered clause

offending_extra_words: and the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction
reasons: Preferred substance is achieved: 28.1 now applies New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County, a permitted corresponding pair, and the Singapore contradiction is removed.

Minimality fails: the operation re-states the forum in 28.1 even though 28.2 already grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County. A tighter edit (swap "Singapore law" for "the laws of the State of New York" and strike the Singapore venue words) would suffice; the operation expands 13 words to 27 and duplicates existing protection.

The pre-existing injunctive-relief carve-out in 28.2 permitting application to "another court with jurisdiction" dilutes exclusivity of the chosen forum; it should be narrowed to the New York County courts, though it is original untouched language rather than an introduced defect.
Intent is preserved: no undefined terms, dangling mechanics, or changes to unrelated commercial terms; the duplication is redundant rather than contradictory.
